messages:
infra-oncall: Heads-up — partial GPU pool eviction in eu-west started at ~12:09 UTC, impact on dedicated nodes. We auto-shifted traffic to other regions per routing policy.
maya: seeing large spike in errors for tokenization-heavy requests routed to ap-southeast. 5xxs climbing.
liam: autoscaler tried to spin up new nodes but quota hit in ap-southeast, provisioning stalled.
anya: also noticing odd DNS behavior: we dropped our API record TTL from 300 -> 60 at 12:05 but many resolvers still returning old A records. Might be caching/sticky resolvers.
maya: confirmed with dig, some resolvers still have the old eu-west IPs.
liam: paste dig outputs:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
198.51.100.23
203.0.113.12
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
203.0.113.12
203.0.113.13
```
maya: looks like mixed sets — sticky cache on some ISPs.
infra-oncall: ops-bot reported CNAME-based steering change applied at 12:06. We changed the region weights to push traffic off eu-west to us-west/ap-southeast.
ops-bot: [ALERT] routing-change: applied weight shift: eu-west 0.0 -> 0.05, us-west 0.5 -> 0.65, ap-southeast 0.5 -> 0.3 (by infra-oncall).
sam: sticky caches + long-lived negative TTLs are causing some clients to keep hitting eu-west, which is starved. That explains why autoscaler in ap-southeast is overwhelmed even though we shifted weights.
anya: to add — some corporate resolvers don't honor low TTLs; we saw a pattern where TTLs get clamped by ISPs to 600 or more. Also EDNS client subnet sometimes expands.
liam: quick mitigation suggestion: add an HTTP-level redirect at eu-west LB to send traffic to /region-handoff with 302 to the closest healthy endpoint. Less dependent on resolver TTLs. Thoughts?
maya: works for public API calls, but internal token exchanges between services use direct A records and will still hit eu-west.
infra-oncall: short-term plan: 1) add HTTP 302 handoff at eu-west for public ingress, 2) manually update CNAME to a short-lived fallback host that some resolvers will pick up, 3) coordinate with CDN to purge edge DNS cache where possible.
sam: also lower our DNS TTL in config to 30s for next 10m and then restore. We need to update the playbook to call out that some resolvers clamp up.
ops-bot: Note: lowering authoritative TTL does not force upstream caches to evict earlier if they already stored higher TTL values — propagation is eventual.
anya: telemetry: query rate for eu-west IPs dropped by only ~40% after the weight shift. That explains the ongoing saturation.
liam: manual capacity step: request emergency quota bump for ap-southeast (TF ticket created) and start spot fallback in us-east as drain target.
maya: putting a short doc snippet in #eng-runtime about sticky resolver checklist and when to do HTTP handoff.
infra-oncall: if quota bump isn't immediate, we will enable connection-limiting and 429 backpressure on eu-west LB to force clients to retry and pick up new records.
sam: reminder — after incident we should run an experiment: set TTL to 5s with a controlled weight change and observe resolver behaviors across major providers, capture which clamp. Add to runbook.
anya: confirmed we will capture dig samples from Cloudflare, Google, ISP A, ISP B and save to incident log.
maya: small config snippet for emergency handoff (example):
```
# nginx on eu-west LB
location / {
  if ($request_uri ~ "^/v1/" ) {
    return 302 https://api-fallback.redwood.ai$request_uri;
  }
}
```
infra-oncall: Action items: @liam request quota, @sam lower TTL+announce, @maya deploy 302 handoff, @anya collect dig samples, ops-bot will post routing-change audit.
ops-bot: [AUDIT] routing-change applied by infra-oncall at 1765007766, TTL-change requested at 1765007900.
liam: quota request in progress, keep me posted if you see sustained 5xxs > 5% over next 10m.
maya: deploying handoff now. Pushing config and will monitor.
anya: dig samples collected: saving to /incidents/1765007777/dig-samples.log
infra-oncall: Good. Once traffic stabilizes we'll revert CNAME trick and restore TTL to 300 and run the TTL clamp experiment later.
maya: after handoff, 5xxs dropped to ~1.2% and redispatch to ap-southeast increased. Still watching latency spikes.
liam: autoscaler now seeing headroom after quota note; new nodes coming up.
infra-oncall: thanks team. Postmortem follow-ups: update DNS failover runbook with sticky resolver appendix, emergency HTTP handoff pattern, and a list of providers known to clamp TTLs.
ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated — partial, monitoring.
